title: LVN Medication-Administration Scope: Sorting the Med Pass (California)
subtitle: 60 y/o post-op client with a mixed order set — the LVN must give what is within scope, coordinate the RN-only tasks, and administer safely
nursesNote: 0800 - 60 y/o female, post-op day 1 on a med-surg unit, alert and oriented. The LVN (IV-certified) is preparing the morning medication pass. Current orders include: oral metoprolol (with pulse/blood-pressure parameters), a subcutaneous enoxaparin injection, oral acetaminophen PRN for mild pain, an IV push dose of furosemide, one unit of packed red blood cells (ordered for a low hemoglobin), and continuation of ordered maintenance IV fluids. Apical pulse 66 and blood pressure 118/72. The LVN practices under the direction of the RN/provider.

steps.title: Recognize Cues
steps.sub: Which tasks are within LVN scope
steps.inst: Select the THREE (3) ordered tasks that are within the California LVN's scope to perform.

opts.text: Administer the oral metoprolol (after checking the pulse and blood-pressure parameters)
opts.rat: Oral medications are within the LVN's scope; the LVN verifies parameters before a rate/pressure-lowering drug.

opts.text: Administer the subcutaneous enoxaparin injection
opts.rat: Subcutaneous injections are within the LVN's scope.

opts.text: Administer the oral acetaminophen PRN for mild pain
opts.rat: Oral PRN medications are within the LVN's scope, given per the client's need and the order.

opts.text: Give the IV push dose of furosemide
opts.rat: IV push medications are outside the California LVN's scope, even with IV certification; the RN administers them.

opts.text: Initiate the ordered blood transfusion
opts.rat: Initiating a blood transfusion is outside the LVN's scope; the RN starts and monitors it.

opts.text: Start and titrate an insulin infusion
opts.rat: Starting/titrating a high-alert IV infusion is outside the LVN's scope; the RN manages it.

opts.text: Develop the client's medication teaching plan for a new diagnosis
opts.rat: Creating the teaching plan is an RN function; the LVN reinforces teaching.

steps.title: Analyze Cues
steps.inst: Select the THREE (3) statements that correctly reflect California LVN scope and safe medication practice.

opts.text: The LVN can administer oral, subcutaneous, intramuscular, and topical medications and, with IV certification, ordered IV fluids, while checking parameters (e.g., pulse/blood pressure before a beta-blocker like metoprolol)
opts.rat: These routes are within scope, and parameter checks are part of safe administration.

opts.text: IV push medications, initiating blood/blood-product transfusions, and starting/titrating high-alert infusions (insulin, heparin, vasopressors) are outside the LVN's scope and are done by the RN
opts.rat: These are clearly outside the California LVN's scope regardless of IV certification.

opts.text: For every medication, the LVN applies the rights of medication administration, uses an independent double-check for high-alert drugs, clarifies unclear orders before giving, and may refuse to give a medication that appears unsafe
opts.rat: These safe-administration practices apply to all medications and protect the client.

opts.text: IV certification allows the LVN to give any medication by any IV route, including IV push
opts.rat: IV certification does not erase scope limits; IV push medications remain outside the LVN's scope.

opts.text: The LVN should give a medication even if the order is unclear, to avoid delaying the med pass
opts.rat: An unclear order is clarified before administration; giving it risks a serious error.

opts.text: Scope of practice does not affect which medications the LVN can give
opts.rat: Scope of practice directly determines which medications/routes the LVN may administer.

steps.title: Prioritize
steps.sub: Rank how the LVN handles the med pass
steps.inst: Drag these actions from HIGHEST priority (1) to LOWEST (5).

opts.text: Verify the pulse and blood-pressure parameters before giving the metoprolol
opts.rat: Checking parameters before a rate/pressure-lowering drug is a safety step that comes first for that medication.

opts.text: Coordinate promptly with the RN so the out-of-scope orders (IV push furosemide, blood transfusion) are carried out and not missed
opts.rat: Ensuring the RN-only orders are done keeps the plan on track and prevents omissions.

opts.text: Administer the in-scope scheduled medications (oral metoprolol within parameters, subcutaneous enoxaparin) at the correct time
opts.rat: Giving the scheduled in-scope medications on time follows the safety checks and coordination.

opts.text: Address the PRN acetaminophen based on the client's need
opts.rat: PRN medication is given as needed and requested — appropriate but lower priority than scheduled meds.

opts.text: Complete documentation of the medications given
opts.rat: Documentation follows administration and is essential but sequenced last.

steps.title: Generate Solutions
steps.inst: Select the THREE (3) actions that are appropriate and within the LVN's scope.

opts.text: Administer the oral metoprolol (within parameters), the subcutaneous enoxaparin, and the PRN acetaminophen, applying the rights of medication administration
opts.rat: These are in-scope routes given with the rights and parameter checks.

opts.text: Notify and coordinate with the RN to perform the out-of-scope orders — the IV push furosemide and the blood transfusion
opts.rat: Coordinating the RN-only tasks ensures they are done safely and not missed.

opts.text: Use an independent double-check for high-alert medications, clarify any unclear order before giving it, and document accurately
opts.rat: These safe-administration practices reduce the risk of harm.

opts.text: Give the IV push furosemide yourself because you are IV certified
opts.rat: IV push remains outside the LVN's scope even with IV certification.

opts.text: Start the blood transfusion to save the RN time
opts.rat: Initiating a blood transfusion is outside the LVN's scope.

opts.text: Give a medication with an unclear order rather than delay the med pass
opts.rat: Unclear orders are clarified first; giving them risks a serious error.

steps.title: Take Action
steps.inst: For the oral metoprolol, drag the steps from FIRST (1) to LAST (5).

opts.text: Verify the order and check for allergies and the pulse/blood-pressure parameters
opts.rat: FIRST — confirm the order, allergies, and the parameters that apply to this drug.

opts.text: Identify the client using two identifiers and measure the apical pulse and blood pressure
opts.rat: SECOND — correct client identification and the parameter measurement precede administration.

opts.text: If within parameters, apply the rights of medication administration and prepare the dose (independent double-check if it is high-alert)
opts.rat: THIRD — proceed only if parameters are met, using the rights and any required double-check.

opts.text: Administer the medication by the correct route and remain to confirm it is taken
opts.rat: FOURTH — give the medication correctly and confirm it is actually taken.

opts.text: Document administration and monitor for the expected effect and any adverse effects
opts.rat: LAST — document and monitor the client's response.

opts.text: The LVN gave the in-scope medications correctly and coordinated the IV push furosemide and blood transfusion with the RN
opts.rat: Correct scope decisions and coordination kept the med pass safe and complete.

opts.text: The LVN checked the apical pulse and blood pressure before the metoprolol, confirmed they were within parameters, and administered it correctly
opts.rat: Verifying parameters before a beta-blocker is correct, safe practice.

opts.text: The LVN gave the IV push furosemide independently because she is IV certified
opts.rat: Administering an IV push medication is outside the California LVN's scope — a scope violation to correct and report.

opts.text: The LVN gave a medication despite an unclear order without clarifying it first
opts.rat: Giving an unclear order without clarification risks a serious medication error and must be corrected.

opts.text: The RN administered the blood transfusion after the LVN's coordination, and the LVN monitored the client within scope
opts.rat: Correct role division: the RN starts the blood; the LVN supports monitoring within scope.

opts.text: The client received the correct medications on time with the rights and a high-alert double-check verified
opts.rat: Timely, correct administration with safety checks is a good outcome.

opts.text: The PRN acetaminophen was held because the client had no pain and did not request it
opts.rat: Appropriately withholding a PRN when it is not needed is correct — no change required.

opts.text: The medication administration record is complete and up to date
opts.rat: An up-to-date record reflects proper documentation with no clinical change.

reference: Aligned to the NCSBN NCLEX-PN Test Plan client-need category: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies (medication administration and expected outcomes) using the NCSBN Clinical Judgment Measurement Model, and supporting an under-weighted LVN blueprint area (Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies is 10-16% of the NCLEX-PN exam). Scope statements reflect the California LVN scope under the Board of Vocational Nursing and Psychiatric Technicians (BVNPT): the LVN administers oral, subcutaneous, intramuscular, topical, and other routine medications and, with IV certification, ordered IV fluids, while verifying parameters (e.g., apical pulse/blood pressure before a beta-blocker) and applying the rights of medication administration with an independent double-check for high-alert drugs; the LVN clarifies unclear orders before administration and may refuse to give a medication that appears unsafe. IV push medications, initiating blood/blood-product transfusions, and starting or titrating high-alert infusions (insulin, heparin, vasopressors) are outside the LVN's scope even with IV certification and are performed by the RN; developing the medication teaching plan is an RN function that the LVN reinforces. Apply within current BVNPT regulations, IV-certification limits, and facility policy, which can change. Lab and vital-sign values use standard reference ranges and are illustrative for the scenario; exact clinical figures are marked for faculty confirmation.
